hourly.summary: United fans are in full injury crisis meltdown mode with Shaw, Dorgu, Sesko and others crocked before October even arrives, forcing Dalot into emergency left-back duty. There's simmering frustration that the Class of '92 pundits (Neville, Scholes, Butt, Keane, Rooney) have gone conspicuously quiet on City's 115 charges — prompting jokes about academy ties — while the blues' 'healthy sustainable business' gets side-eyed. The only cheer comes from gallows humour about United and Liverpool bonding over City 'cooking the books' and a nostalgic nod to Amorim's Sporting days.

daily.summary: The day began with intense schadenfreude (8/10) over Manchester City's 115 charges, but sentiment plummeted steadily as self-loathing over United's own Glazer-era dysfunction crept in, cynicism about football's governance took hold, and a derby humiliation sealed a collapse into existential despair (2/10).

weekly.summary: Manchester United fan sentiment remained locked in a profound, unrelenting crisis throughout the week, with daily scores clustered at 2-3/10 and no meaningful improvement. The mood deepened from post-derby outrage and Carabao Cup collapse into a settled, existential conviction that the club is structurally broken — encompassing ownership (INEOS/Glazers), management (Carrick), recruitment, identity, and physical conditioning. A fleeting shift to 'resigned' despair mid-week only underscored the fatigue of repeated cycles, before sentiment plunged back to 'catastrophic' and 'crisis' lows.
